IB 2027 | SL | Unit 1

B1.2 Computational Thinking

Turn complex problems into solvable structures

Cluster A | Abstraction + decomposition

How do we control complexity without losing meaning?

A school transport app fails because route planning, payment, and safeguarding all collide in one design.

Where do abstraction and decomposition begin?

I do

Model both moves on one scenario

Computational thinking move Modeled action
Abstraction Ignore bus paint color and focus on capacity, stop time, and route order.
Decomposition Split problem into sign-up, route allocation, and live delay alerts.

Abstraction chooses what matters. Decomposition chooses where work is separated.

We do

Decide what stays and what splits

Given a clinic booking platform, identify:

  • Two details to remove through abstraction
  • Three sub-problems to create through decomposition

You do

Worksheet handoff

You Do: Complete the abstraction and decomposition worksheet in Activities.

Apply both decisions to a fresh scenario and justify each choice.

Cluster B | Pattern recognition + algorithmic thinking

When should we reuse and when should we sequence?

Pattern recognition finds repeatable structure; algorithmic thinking turns it into precise steps.

How do we avoid repeating work and still keep logic exact?

I do

Model the combined approach

Scenario: markbook processing for every class.

  • Pattern recognition: each class follows the same validation and grade-band logic.
  • Algorithmic thinking: define a finite ordered sequence for import, validation, grade rule, and report output.

The reusable pattern gives structure; the algorithmic thinking prevents ambiguity.

We do

Transfer to a new domain

Pick one domain and explain both moves:

  • Machine learning
  • Network monitoring
  • Online retail search

State the pattern first, then draft the ordered algorithmic thinking steps.

Cluster C | Across CS domains

Can the four pillars explain real system design choices?

Use abstraction, decomposition, pattern recognition, and algorithmic thinking to analyze software, machine learning, networks, and databases.

I do

Map pillars to domains

Domain Best pillar entry Why it matters
Software systems Decomposition Enables modular teams and clearer responsibility boundaries.
Machine learning Pattern recognition Finds useful signal in high-volume training data.
Networks Abstraction Layer models hide low-level complexity for better reasoning.
Databases Algorithmic thinking Query and indexing strategies rely on explicit, ordered logic.

We do

Challenge the mapping

Take one row from the table and argue an alternative pillar as the primary lens.

What changes in design decisions if you switch that lens?

You do

Worksheet handoff

You Do: Complete the domain transfer worksheet in Activities.

Explain one problem in each domain using all four pillars.

Synthesis

If one pillar were removed, which system would fail first and why?

Choose software, machine learning, networks, or databases and defend the failure pathway with precise reasoning.
